name: Local gym A/B: hockey strength and shoulder tolerance
summary: 12 full-body sessions, at most 2 a week, alternating A (bilateral and posterior chain) and B (single-leg and hip control).
notes:
12 full-body sessions for hockey strength and shoulder tolerance.

Structure: at most 2 gym visits a week. Alternate A and B whenever you attend, normally with at least 48 hours between gym sessions. If you miss a visit, continue the sequence without catching up. Progress by recovery and symptoms, not by elapsed time.

Priorities: leg and hip strength for skating; single-leg strength and pelvic control; hamstring and adductor capacity; upper-back, rotator-cuff and scapular control; keep pressing strength without disproportionate pressing volume; preserve muscle during weight loss.

Every session, prepare with: easy stationary cycling; dynamic hip and ankle mobility; your prescribed shoulder preparation; a progressive exercise-specific warm-up.

Shoulders: build capacity rather than just pulling the shoulders back. Each session has one row and one extra back or rear-shoulder exercise alongside one press; this balance is a programming choice, not a proven injury-prevention ratio. Let the shoulder blades move naturally; do not force them back and down on every exercise. Integrate your prescribed rehab exercises without duplicating their workload. Optional support work where compatible with your rehab: supported cable or band external rotation (rotator cuff), serratus wall slide (upward rotation and control). Modify aggravating exercises: shoulder pain, movement and function should not be worse the next morning. Returning night pain, restricted movement or new weakness needs clinical reassessment.

Hockey: avoid demanding leg training immediately before hockey, and reduce lower-body demand when training within the 24 hours before.

plans.name: Local gym A: bilateral strength and posterior chain
plans.description: Bilateral strength and posterior chain. Alternate with B.

exercises.notes: Quadriceps and glute strength. Sets and reps are a starting default (the source plan says they are still to follow): stop with 2-3 reps in reserve and choose loads you can repeat with good technique.
Hamstrings and hip-extension strength. Swap: cable pull-through if holding dumbbells aggravates the shoulders.
Upper-back strength with limited trunk fatigue.
Pressing strength with a limited bottom range. Use a tolerated grip and range; your 80+ kg bench does not set the starting load. Swap: whichever press is better tolerated, or omit temporarily.
Rear-deltoid and scapular-retractor capacity. Swap: comfortable cable reverse fly, or omit if aggravating.
Trunk resistance to rotation; reps per side. Swap: dead bug if the cable position irritates the shoulder.

plans.name: Local gym B: single-leg strength and hip control
plans.description: Single-leg strength and hip control. Alternate with A.

exercises.notes: Single-leg strength and pelvic control; reps per leg. Swap: single-leg leg press if balance or holding weights is limiting. Sets and reps are a starting default (the source plan says they are still to follow): stop with 2-3 reps in reserve and choose loads you can repeat with good technique.

exercises.exercise_name: Seated cable row with independent handles
exercises.notes: Back strength through a comfortable shoulder path.
Controlled pressing with an adjustable starting position. Swap: whichever press is better tolerated, or omit temporarily.
Vertical pulling in front, through a tolerated overhead range. Swap: supported row if overhead pulling aggravates symptoms.
Trunk control during limb movement; reps per side.

sessions.note: Session 1 of 12: Establish comfortable ranges and baseline tolerance.
Session 2 of 12: Establish single-leg control and machine settings.
Session 3 of 12: Repeat baseline and assess recovery.
Session 4 of 12: Confirm tolerance before progression.
Session 5 of 12: Begin gradual strength progression.
Session 6 of 12: Develop single-leg and hip strength.
Session 7 of 12: Progress legs and upper back while controlling pressing demand.
Session 8 of 12: Consolidate unilateral strength and adductor tolerance.
Session 9 of 12: Continue progression where symptoms and technique remain stable.
Session 10 of 12: Develop strength while preserving hockey recovery.
Session 11 of 12: Compare with session 1 without maximum testing.
Session 12 of 12: Compare with session 2 and select the next training block.
